appSourceFacts: CafeWorld acquisition effect cleanup calls host release, removes tap/window listeners on effect cleanup.
Escape removes only Immersive holder; remaining Player holder receives the same canvas, so this is not last-holder release.
CafeHost does not override disposeDelayMs; last-holder release stops RAF, disconnects ResizeObserver, removes canvas, and schedules teardown after default5000ms.

Teardown clears host ownership before engine.dispose. CafeEngine.dispose stops RAF, removes context-loss listener, disposes reflector/refraction/environment/world/renderer, forces context loss, marks lifecycle disposed.
Native session stop selects list/feedback and playback idle; Player rendering is conditional on viewMode player, so it supplies an observable actual unmount path.

facts: Client context.close awaits channel close and its closed promise.
BrowserServer.close maps to owned browserProcess.close; Chromium graceful close sends Browser.close on its pipe transport, then waits child close and temporary-directory cleanup.
The public close has its own default30000ms closeOrKill path; this suite enforces the explicit shorter10000ms gate, which was not relaxed.
BrowserServer.kill maps to recorded detached own process-group SIGKILL and waits cleanup; own child exit plus kill acknowledgement were recorded.
connect() marks browser.close as disconnect-only; it is distinct from BrowserServer.close.

oneProposedComparison.description: Keep the same binary/flags/build/context+server close bounds. After a short normal Cafe startup, retain only a read-only canvas handle, use actual visible Session End button, observe disconnected canvas and stopped frame counter, wait through documented5000ms idle retention for lifecycle=disposed; then context.close and server.close with separate send/ack timestamps and own PID/exit logging. No synthetic dispatch, engine calls, renderer/quality edits or larger cleanup deadline.
discriminators: If native unmount never reaches lifecycle disposed, that is a concrete application lifecycle failure requiring owner review.
If lifecycle disposed is observed but the same BrowserServer timeout remains, the failure is demonstrably after the application teardown path completed; it is not evidence that dispose never ran.

If both app teardown and server close pass, evidence only shows this explicit-unmount sequence differs from the completed abrupt document-close sequence; it does not prove an application bug or erase the prior failure.
